final.name: Practiced caption compression
final.audit_justification: It primarily measures practiced compression and caption form rather than the effectiveness or cartoon-specific substance of the joke, though practice could also improve genuine writing quality.

final.name: Transcription artifacts
final.audit_justification: These are transcription and cataloging artifacts unrelated to the caption's comic substance.

final.name: Verbose conversational filler
final.audit_justification: Filler and run-on phrasing measure verbosity and conversational surface habits rather than caption quality.

final.name: Topical Reference Self-Sufficiency
final.audit_justification: The caption's dependence on external references directly affects the substance and accessibility of its humor.

final.name: Secondary-detail leverage
final.audit_justification: Using secondary visual details as part of the joke is direct evidence of cartoon-specific observation and construction.

final.name: Generic caption polish
final.audit_justification: Generic setup-punch polish is a template or practice marker rather than proof of a good fit, though practiced writers may also produce better captions.

final.name: Bureaucratic or corporate jargon usage
final.audit_justification: Corporate or bureaucratic vocabulary is a subject-matter marker whose presence alone says nothing about quality.

final.name: Layered semantic convergence
final.audit_justification: Clean convergence of multiple meanings on the depicted situation is substantive evidence of comic construction.

final.name: Extreme conversational brevity
final.audit_justification: Extreme brevity is a length and delivery-style feature, not quality by itself.

final.name: Payoff surprise
final.audit_justification: A coherent surprise at the payoff is direct evidence about the caption's comic effectiveness.

final.name: Generic-prior obvious idiom
final.audit_justification: Reliance on an obvious visual idiom primarily marks generic or cliché association without assessing its execution.

final.name: Speaker-role fidelity
final.audit_justification: Plausibility for a depicted speaker directly concerns how well the caption fits the cartoon.

final.name: Pun and idiom density
final.audit_justification: Wordplay density describes a stylistic technique without judging whether the wordplay is apt or effective.

final.name: Petty-Stakes Emotional Grounding
final.audit_justification: Specific, relatable emotional investment is substantive characterization and comic grounding for the depicted scene.

final.name: Conversational punch timing
final.audit_justification: Setup and payoff timing directly measures whether the caption delivers its comic turn effectively.

final.name: Topical news cycle reference
final.audit_justification: Contemporary named references are temporal and topical markers whose specificity does not itself establish quality.

final.name: Non-template angle
final.audit_justification: A surprising individualized angle rather than a stock response is direct evidence of originality and fit.

final.name: House-style tonal register
final.audit_justification: Plain understated diction primarily signals a house or community style and is not inherently good for a particular cartoon.

final.name: Freshness over cliché
final.audit_justification: Transforming familiar material into a fresh comic idea directly bears on originality and execution.

final.name: Deadpan Underreaction To Surreal Danger
final.audit_justification: Treating surreal danger as mundane is a substantive comedic stance tied directly to the depicted situation.

final.name: Setup-to-Payoff Register Shift
final.audit_justification: A coherent register shift from setup to payoff directly measures the caption's comic structure and effectiveness.
